# USR-004: sudoers is root owned and NOPASSWD entries are deliberate

- **Group:** Users and privilege
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

A sudoers file that anyone but root can write is a direct escalation to root. NOPASSWD entries are sometimes required (a PaaS deploy account) but are the first thing an attacker with a user shell uses, so they are listed so each one is a decision.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ls -l /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d; sudo visudo -c
```

## How to fix it

Fix ownership and mode (`chown root:root`, `chmod 0440`), validate with `visudo -cf <file>`, and keep NOPASSWD to the PaaS account.

## What a fix can break

Removing a NOPASSWD line breaks whatever automation relied on it.

Run `stackward explain USR-004` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
